# `sort` standard library

`sort` provides collection sorting helpers. The typed helpers `sort::ints` and
`sort::strings` use a hybrid merge sort ($O(n \log n)$ time complexity) that copies
their input into a new growable array and leaves the original unchanged.
The low-level `raw_sort_slots` engine uses in-place quadratic insertion sort ($O(n^2)$ worst case).

| Export | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `Strings` | `String{}` | growable string-array type |
| `Ints` | `Int{}` | growable integer-array type |
| `strings` | `Strings => Strings` | ascending `str::cmp` order ($O(n \log n)$ hybrid merge sort) |
| `ints` | `Ints => Ints` | ascending numeric order ($O(n \log n)$ hybrid merge sort) |
| `raw_sort_slots` | `Int, (Int, Int => <>), (Int, Int => Int) => ()` | callback-driven in-place slot engine ($O(n^2)$ insertion sort) |

```{.dva .run}
#use io
#use sort

numbers = sort::Ints()
numbers += 9
numbers += 2
numbers += 5
ordered = sort::ints(numbers)
io::out(ordered(0)!!)
// => 2
```

`raw_sort_slots` accepts an element count, an index comparator `(i, j) => <>`, and a
swap callback `(i, j) => Int`; the caller owns the storage that those callbacks access.
